statements.text: With continued passage, deermouse fibroblasts spontaneously became a stable cell line, whereas the mouse fibroblast population lost viability.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: With continued passage, the mouse cell population lost viability, while the deermouse cell population spontaneously transformed into a cell line stably maintained under standard conditions.
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this divergence in behaviour on continued passage.

statements.text: Among transcribed ERV/TE sequences, those in P. leucopus cells were longer and more translatable than those in M. musculus cells.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The transcribed ERV/TE sequences in M. musculus cells were generally longer in length and had greater potential for translation than sequences in treated P. leucopus cells.
statements.note: The direction is reversed: the longer, more translatable sequences were in mouse cells, not deermouse cells.

statements.text: Deermouse fibroblasts carry fewer endogenous retrovirus copies in their genome than mouse fibroblasts.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In the cultures of both species, there was increased transcription of several types of endogenous retrovirus (ERV) and transposable elements (TEs) after exposure to the agonist.
statements.note: Only transcription after agonist exposure is reported; genomic ERV copy number in the two species is never compared.

statements.text: Single-cell RNA-seq showed that each species' cultures contained at least two fibroblast types, which differed in their responses to TLR agonists.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: By single-cell RNA-seq, cultures of both species comprised at least two types of fibroblasts, which were further differentiated in their responses to TLR agonists.
statements.note: This restates the single-cell finding, including the minimum count of two fibroblast types.

statements.text: Patients with ESR1-mutant EV-DNA achieved longer progression-free survival when switched from fulvestrant to a PI3K inhibitor.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Baseline ESR1 mutations in EV-DNA were associated with shorter progression-free survival (PFS) across the cohort, with the Y537S mutation showing a particularly strong impact on the outcome of fulvestrant-treated patients.
statements.note: The study is prognostic: it reports outcomes by mutation status, not the effect of changing treatment.

statements.text: Across the cohort, PIK3CA mutations were detected in 22% of patients and ESR1 mutations in 25%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: PIK3CA and ESR1 mutations were found in 22 and 25% of patients.
statements.note: These are the two detection frequencies the abstract gives.

statements.text: Patients whose EV-DNA carried ESR1 mutations at baseline had shorter progression-free survival, with Y537S hitting fulvestrant-treated patients hardest.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Baseline ESR1 mutations in EV-DNA were associated with shorter progression-free survival (PFS) across the cohort, with the Y537S mutation showing a particularly strong impact on the outcome of fulvestrant-treated patients.
statements.note: Both the cohort-wide association and the Y537S effect in fulvestrant-treated patients are reported.

statements.text: PIK3CA mutations measured in EV-DNA correlated significantly with progression-free survival in this cohort.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In contrast, PIK3CA mutations in EV-DNA did not significantly correlate with PFS, whereas in ctDNA, they were linked to poor outcomes.
statements.note: Significance is flipped: in EV-DNA the PIK3CA association with PFS was explicitly non-significant.

statements.text: The study assembled 747 complete plasmid sequences carrying bla OXA-48-like genes from the NCBI database.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We systematically collected 747 complete plasmid sequences carrying bla OXA-48-like genes from the NCBI database
statements.note: The sample size of 747 complete plasmids is stated directly.

statements.text: bla OXA-181 was the predominant variant in Europe, while bla OXA-48 prevailed in South Asia.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: with bla OXA-48 predominating in Europe, bla OXA-181 in South Asia, and bla OXA-232 largely in Asia
statements.note: The two regions are swapped: OXA-48 predominated in Europe and OXA-181 in South Asia.

statements.text: Sixteen transmission units were delimited, and AA068_Cluster3 was dated to the Netherlands around 2005 before it expanded to other regions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Sixteen transmission units were defined, with AA068_Cluster3 estimated to have originated in the Netherlands around 2005 before expanding to Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and North America.
statements.note: Both the count of transmission units and the dating of AA068_Cluster3 are reported.

statements.text: Carriage of bla OXA-48-like plasmids raises mortality among patients with bloodstream infections.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The spread of OXA-48-like carbapenemases represents a major public health challenge.
statements.note: The analysis is plasmid-genomic; no patient outcomes such as mortality are examined.

statements.text: The cobas EGFR test reached a lower limit of detection with K2EDTA tubes than with Roche cfDNA tubes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Overall, test performance was equally robust with either blood collection tube, eg, regarding limit of detection, linearity, and reproducibility, making Roche cfDNA tubes suitable for routine clinical laboratory use in this setting.
statements.note: Performance including limit of detection was equally robust with both tubes, not better with K2EDTA.

statements.text: Limit of detection, linearity and reproducibility of the cobas EGFR test were comparable whichever of the two collection tubes was used.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Overall, test performance was equally robust with either blood collection tube, eg, regarding limit of detection, linearity, and reproducibility, making Roche cfDNA tubes suitable for routine clinical laboratory use in this setting.
statements.note: This is the headline equivalence result for the three named performance measures.

statements.text: Roche cfDNA tubes cost more per sample than standard K2EDTA tubes.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Importantly, the Roche cfDNA tubes provided more flexibility for specimen handling versus K2EDTA tubes, eg, in terms of tube mixing, plasma separation, and sample stability
statements.note: The tubes are compared on handling and stability only; price is never mentioned either way.

statements.text: Roche cfDNA Collection Tubes keep whole blood stable for as long as 7 days before plasma separation, whereas K2EDTA tubes demand separation within 4 to 8 hours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Standard K2EDTA tubes require plasma separation from blood within 4 to 8 hours; however, Roche Cell-Free DNA (cfDNA) Collection Tubes (Roche cfDNA tube) enable whole blood stability for up to 7 days prior to plasma separation.
statements.note: Both stability windows are given with these exact figures.

statements.text: Mean total cfDNA concentration was about 15 pg/uL in esophageal carcinoma patients versus about 6 pg/uL in healthy donors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Total cfDNA concentration was significantly higher in patients than in healthy donors (15.03 ± 1.37 vs. 5.87 ± 0.85 pg/μL, p < .0001).
statements.note: The two group means reported are 15.03 and 5.87 pg/uL.

statements.text: Total cfDNA concentration fell after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in these esophageal carcinoma patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings support further longitudinal evaluation to determine the predictive and prognostic value of cfDNA in locally advanced unresectable esophageal carcinoma.
statements.note: Only a single comparison of patients with controls is reported; on-treatment measurements are called for, not made.

statements.text: Plasma cfDNA fragments were significantly longer in patients with esophageal carcinoma than in healthy donors.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Additionally, we observed a significant reduction in patients fragment length compared to healthy donors.
statements.note: Fragment length was significantly reduced, not increased, in patients.

statements.text: At a 7.5 pg/uL cut-off, total cfDNA concentration separated patients from healthy donors with 81% sensitivity and 80% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The threshold of 7.5 pg/μL yielded a sensitivity of 81% and a specificity of 80%.
statements.note: These are the exact threshold and performance figures given.

statements.text: A prospective cohort of 38 patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma receiving immunotherapy was analysed.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A cohort of 38 advanced HCC patients receiving immunotherapy was prospectively analyzed.
statements.note: The cohort size of 38 and its prospective design are stated.

statements.text: Patients whose best radiological response was progressive disease carried significantly more copy number variations than patients who responded.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients with progressive disease (PD) as their best radiological response had significantly fewer copy number variations (CNVs) than those with a radiological response.
statements.note: The direction is inverted: progressive-disease patients had fewer CNVs, not more.

statements.text: Baseline cell-free DNA and circulating tumour DNA levels distinguished patients according to their radiological response to checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Baseline levels of cfDNA and ctDNA effectively discriminated HCC patients based on their radiological response to ICIs.
statements.note: This is the reported discriminative performance of baseline cfDNA and ctDNA.

statements.text: CDKN2A mutations in circulating tumour DNA predicted which patients would show a radiological response to checkpoint inhibitors.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Additionally, individuals with pathologic mutations in the CDKN2A gene exhibited significantly reduced survival.
statements.note: CDKN2A is tied to survival only; its relation to radiological response is a different endpoint that is not reported.

statements.text: Detectable ctDNA mutations were more common in patients with well-differentiated pancreatic tumours.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Detectable ctDNA mutations were more frequent in patients with poorly differentiated tumors
statements.note: The association runs the other way: detection was more frequent in poorly differentiated tumours.

statements.text: Patients without detectable ctDNA mutations survived longer, with median survival of 18 months versus 10.5 months.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: patients without detectable ctDNA mutations showed longer survival (medians of 10.5 months vs. 18 months, p = 0.019)
statements.note: The survival advantage for ctDNA-negative patients and both median values are reported.

statements.text: Mutations detected in plasma matched those found in the matched resected tumour tissue in most patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study explores ctDNA detection by next generation sequencing (NGS) and associated clinicopathologic factors in patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
statements.note: Only plasma was sequenced; no tissue-to-plasma concordance analysis is described.

statements.text: Detectable mutations in KRAS and/or TP53 were found in 25 patients, 30.9% of those analysed, at allele frequencies of 0.05 to 8.5%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Twenty-five patients (30.9%) had detectable mutations in KRAS and/or TP53 with allele frequencies ranging from 0.05 to 8.5%
statements.note: The count, percentage and allele-frequency range are all given.

statements.text: The study found high UBE2C expression in gliomas to be a factor promoting the malignant phenotype of tumour cells.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The results suggests that the high expression and risk of UBE2C in gliomas may be a factor that promotes malignant phenotype of tumor cells.
statements.note: This is the central conclusion drawn about UBE2C expression and malignancy.

statements.text: Knocking down UBE2C extended survival in mouse glioma xenografts.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: UBE2C were evaluated by clinical grading, survival prognosis and cell experiments.
statements.note: Survival was assessed from patient data and experiments were done in cells; no animal model appears in the abstract.

statements.text: IL6 and IL10 were identified as the key nodes driving an immune-activated, rather than immunosuppressive, phenotype in glioma.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The immune phenotype shows that IL6 and IL10 may be the key nodes affecting the immunosuppressive phenotype of glioma.
statements.note: The phenotype is inverted: IL6 and IL10 are tied to immunosuppression, not immune activation.

statements.text: MMP-family invasiveness genes, MMP2 and MMP9 in particular, were correlated with immunosuppressive phenotypes through the UBE2C-IL6/IL10 axis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Further, the tumor cells aggressive genes from the MMP family can be correlated with immunosuppressive phenotypes via UBE2C-IL6/IL10 axis, especially displayed by MMP2/MMP9.
statements.note: The MMP-to-immunosuppression link via the UBE2C-IL6/IL10 axis is reported, with MMP2/MMP9 highlighted.

statements.text: Deleting the comM gene made Acinetobacter baumannii more susceptible to carbapenems.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: One integration site is within the comM gene and coincides with the previously described Tn6022 elements suggested to account for the AbaR resistance island.
statements.note: comM is described only as an integration site; no antibiotic susceptibility testing is reported.

statements.text: Transposition of Tn6022 into the comM attachment site was reproduced in E. coli, which also revealed use of a novel transposition protein.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We established Tn6022 in a heterologous E. coli host and confirmed basic features of transposition into the comM attachment site and the use of a novel transposition protein.
statements.note: Both the heterologous transposition into comM and the novel transposition protein are confirmed findings.

statements.text: The two newly identified diversification mechanisms could not be shown to be active in E. coli.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The activities of these diversification features were confirmed in E. coli.
statements.note: Their activities were in fact confirmed in E. coli.

statements.text: Four distinct families of Tn7-like transposons were identified in Acinetobacter baumannii, each recognising a different integration site.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We analyzed the contribution of Tn7-like transposons to island formation and diversification in the nosocomial pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii and identified four separate families that recognize different integration sites.
statements.note: The count of four families with distinct integration sites is stated directly.

statements.text: After acquisition, the Tox island is frequently lost and rarely persists in the genome.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Once acquired, the Tox island tends to be stably maintained, evolving with the genome.
statements.note: Stable maintenance is reported, the opposite of frequent loss.

statements.text: The Pht cluster was acquired on seven separate occasions, by four P. syringae phylogroups and by the rhizobacterium Pseudomonas sp. JAI115.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The Pht cluster has been acquired, either naked or associated with a GInt, on seven independent occasions by four phylogroups of P. syringae and the distant rhizobacterium Pseudomonas sp. JAI115.
statements.note: Seven independent acquisitions across four phylogroups plus JAI115 are reported.

statements.text: Strains carrying the Pht cluster cause more severe lesions on their host plants than strains lacking it.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings underscore the potential role of phaseolotoxin in bacterial fitness and contribute to our understanding of virulence evolution in plant pathogens.
statements.note: A possible fitness role is inferred from the evolutionary analysis; no infection experiment comparing strains is described.

statements.text: Three different GInt elements captured the Pht cluster independently of one another.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The Pht cluster was independently captured by three distinct GInt elements, suggesting specific mechanisms for gene capture.
statements.note: Three independent capture events by distinct GInt elements are reported.

statements.text: Fibroblasts and endothelial cells became less abundant while T cells and B cells increased as cervical squamous cell carcinoma developed.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We found that fibroblasts and endothelial cells decreased, whereas immune cells (mainly T cells and B cells) increased during CSCC development.
statements.note: This is the reported cell-composition shift across the progression cascade.

statements.text: PTGDS promotes CSCC progression, whereas CLDN1 and ISG15 suppress it.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: CLDN1 and ISG15 promote CSCC progression, whereas PTGDS suppresses it.
statements.note: The roles are swapped: CLDN1 and ISG15 are the promoters and PTGDS the suppressor.

statements.text: A three-gene panel of CLDN1, ISG15 and PTGDS was identified as clinically significant for the precancer-to-cancer transition.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Additionally, a panel of gene signatures (CLDN1, ISG15, PTGDS) with clinical significance for the precise diagnosis and personalized treatment strategies of PCT was identified.
statements.note: The panel and its three member genes are reported as a result.

statements.text: Patients with high ISG15 expression benefit from adding FGFR1 inhibitors to chemoradiotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: FGFR1 and PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitors were found to suppress CSCC cell proliferation in vitro and tumor growth in vivo.
statements.note: Inhibitors were tested in cells and animals; no biomarker-stratified patient treatment result is reported.

statements.text: The nine-gene index was distilled from a 112-gene candidate pool in a TCGA cohort of 243 MMRp/MSS tumours with 39 deaths.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: IEI was derived from a 112-gene biologically constrained candidate pool using Cox elastic-net modeling in the TCGA candidate MMRp/MSS cohort (243 tumors, 39 death events).
statements.note: The candidate pool size, cohort size and event count are all given.

statements.text: Patients with a low immune exclusion index responded to pembrolizumab monotherapy in this cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Mismatch repair-proficient or microsatellite stable (MMRp/MSS) endometrial cancer derives limited benefit from immune checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy
statements.note: Limited checkpoint-inhibitor benefit is background; no patient in the analysis is reported as treated or evaluated for response.

statements.text: Higher index values were associated with worse overall survival, with an unadjusted hazard ratio of 5.06 that fell to 2.00 after adjustment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The weighted 9-gene IEI showed apparent association with poor overall survival in the same TCGA cohort (unadjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 5.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.80-9.14, p = 7.77e-08; adjusted HR = 2.00, 95% CI 1.37-2.93, p = 3.62e-04)
statements.note: Both the unadjusted and adjusted hazard ratios are reported with these values.

statements.text: The Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts provided independent validation of the index's survival association in MMRp/MSS tumours.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts supported the adverse phenotype direction but not independent MMRp/MSS survival validation; CPTAC and GSE251923 supported RNA-protein and spot-level marker consistency.
statements.note: The GEO cohorts explicitly did not deliver independent MMRp/MSS survival validation.

statements.text: PtGtsf1 binds the PIWI protein Ptiwi09 and Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 and is required for PIWI-dependent elimination of transposon DNA during sexual development.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: PtGtsf1 interacts with PIWI (Ptiwi09) and Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 and is essential for PIWI-dependent DNA elimination of transposons during sexual development.
statements.note: Both interaction partners and the requirement for transposon DNA elimination are reported.

statements.text: PtGtsf1 is dispensable for the degradation of PIWI-bound small RNAs that match Paramecium's own genomic sequences.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: PtGtsf1 is crucial for the degradation of PIWI-bound small RNAs that recognize the organism's own genomic sequences.
statements.note: PtGtsf1 is described as crucial for that degradation, not dispensable.

statements.text: The piRNA pathway in Paramecium silences transposons through DNA methylation of their sequences.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Without PtGtsf1, self-matching small RNAs are not degraded and results in an accumulation of H3K9me3 and H3K27me3, which may disturb transposon recognition.
statements.note: Only histone modifications are measured; DNA methylation is neither reported nor ruled out.

statements.text: In cells lacking PtGtsf1, small RNAs matching the organism's own genome persist and H3K9me3 and H3K27me3 build up.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Without PtGtsf1, self-matching small RNAs are not degraded and results in an accumulation of H3K9me3 and H3K27me3, which may disturb transposon recognition.
statements.note: This restates the reported consequence of PtGtsf1 loss.

statements.text: Subtomogram averaging produced a map of the immature HERV-K capsid at 3.2 A resolution, in which hexamers are held together by a six-helix bundle.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The resulting cryoET STA map of the immature HERV-K capsid at 3.2 Å resolution shows a hexamer unit oligomerized through a 6-helix bundle which is further stabilized by a small molecule in the same way as the IP6 in immature HIV-1 capsid.
statements.note: The resolution and the six-helix-bundle hexamer architecture are both reported.

statements.text: Capsid assembly inhibitors developed from this structure reduced HERV-K expression in neurons from patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Human endogenous retrovirus K (HERV-K) is the most recently acquired endogenous retrovirus, is activated and expressed in many cancers and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and possibly contributes to the aging process.
statements.note: ALS appears only as background motivation; no inhibitors or patient-derived cells are studied.

statements.text: Maturation of the HERV-K capsid protein involves no major conformational change, unlike the maturation of HIV-1.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A large conformational change mediated by the flexible linker between the N-terminal and the C-terminal domains of CA occurs between the immature and the mature HERV-K capsid protein, analogous to HIV-1.
statements.note: A large conformational change is reported, and it is described as analogous to HIV-1 rather than unlike it.

statements.text: HERV-K particles leave a larger gap between viral membrane and immature capsid lattice than other retroviruses, matching extra SP1 and p15 peptides between CA and MA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The HERV-K VLPs show a greater distance between the viral membrane and immature capsid lattice, correlating with the presence of additional peptides, SP1 and p15, between the capsid (CA) and matrix (MA) proteins compared to the other retroviruses.
statements.note: The greater membrane-to-lattice distance and its correlation with the extra SP1 and p15 peptides are reported.

statements.text: Progression-free survival superiority was seen in the breast and kidney baskets, while the pancreas and prostate baskets were inconclusive.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Within each basket, PFS superiority was identified for the pancreas, prostate, and other baskets, whereas the breast and kidney baskets were inconclusive.
statements.note: The baskets are swapped: pancreas and prostate showed superiority, breast and kidney were inconclusive.

statements.text: Radiotherapy delivered the metastasis-directed therapy for 98% of treated metastases, 370 of 379.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Radiotherapy was used as MDT for 98% of metastases (370/379).
statements.note: The proportion and the underlying counts are stated.

statements.text: Adding metastasis-directed therapy to standard-of-care systemic therapy improved progression-free survival overall, with a hazard ratio of 0.54.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Overall, after a median follow-up of 53 months, PFS was improved with MDT + SOC (hazard ratio [HR], 0.54 [95% CI, 0.41 to 0.72], P < .001).
statements.note: This is the trial's primary result with the hazard ratio as reported.

statements.text: Overall survival across all baskets was significantly longer with metastasis-directed therapy added to standard of care.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: PFS, the primary end point, was prespecified in the per-protocol set within each basket, across all baskets, and across all baskets excluding the prostate baskets.
statements.note: PFS was the primary endpoint; survival appears only as a correlate of ctDNA status, never compared between the two randomised arms.

statements.text: DEFB1 was expressed most strongly in salivary gland, kidney and pancreas tissue.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: DEFB1 expression was highest in salivary glands, kidneys, and pancreas.
statements.note: These are the three tissues named as having highest expression.

statements.text: High DEFB1 expression predicted worse overall survival in lung and pancreatic adenocarcinoma but better survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: High DEFB1 expression was linked to poorer overall survival in lung adenocarcinoma and pancreatic adenocarcinoma, but better survival in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
statements.note: The opposite prognostic directions in these cancer types are reported.

statements.text: DEFB1 expression in tumours is driven by hypermethylation of its promoter.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Additionally, we examined DEFB1 genetic alterations, immune cell infiltration, and its molecular partners using various bioinformatics tools.
statements.note: Genetic alterations and infiltration were surveyed; promoter methylation is not among the analyses described.

statements.text: DEFB1 was found to be upregulated in breast, colon and rectal cancers.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In cancers, DEFB1 was upregulated in cholangiocarcinoma, kidney chromophobe, and melanoma, but downregulated in breast, colon, and rectal cancers.
statements.note: In exactly those three cancers DEFB1 was downregulated, not upregulated.

statements.text: Expressing IS608 TnpB raised transposon activity roughly fivefold relative to cells lacking TnpB.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: it is demonstrated that the expression of TnpB of IS608 results in ~5x increased transposon activity compared to cells lacking TnpB expression
statements.note: The approximately fivefold increase with TnpB expression is the quantified result.

statements.text: TnpB raises IS608 transposition by increasing the level of the IS608 transposase protein.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The effects of TnpB on the transposition rates of IS608 are quantified
statements.note: The rate increase is measured, but no mechanism by which TnpB produces it is examined.

statements.text: IS608 belongs to the IS200/IS605 family, whose members are rare in bacterial genomes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The IS200/IS605 family of transposable elements are abundant mobile elements connected with one of the most innumerable genes found in nature, tnpB.
statements.note: The family is described as abundant, with tnpB among the most numerous genes in nature.

statements.text: Transposition of IS608 was followed in living bacterial cells using fluorescent reporters coupled to transposition.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Here, a protocol is outlined to perform live, real-time imaging of transposable element activity in live bacterial cells using a suite of fluorescent reporters coupled to transposition.
statements.note: This describes the imaging approach the protocol sets out.

statements.text: Screening retained 375 shared differentially expressed genes, which mapped to 114 GO terms and 28 KEGG pathways.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Differential expression screening retained 375 shared DEGs. Functional enrichment identified 114 significant GO terms and 28 significant KEGG pathways (p <0.05).
statements.note: All three counts are reported exactly.

statements.text: Immune cell fractions, including M0 macrophages and plasma cells, did not differ significantly between high- and low-PLG tumours.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: CIBERSORT analysis further demonstrated significant differences in resting dendritic cells, resting mast cells, plasma cells, M0 macrophages, and activated memory CD4⁺ T cells between the high- and low-PLG-expression groups (p <0.05).
statements.note: Significance is flipped: those fractions differed significantly between the PLG expression groups.

statements.text: Serum plasminogen protein levels distinguish ccRCC patients from healthy individuals.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Plasminogen (PLG) emerged as the core candidate associated with survival and clinicopathological stage (p <0.05).
statements.note: PLG was identified from tumour RNA-sequencing data; no serum protein measurement is reported.

statements.text: The analysis used RNA-sequencing data from 601 patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma in TCGA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RNA-sequencing data from 601 patients with ccRCC in the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analysed using R.
statements.note: The cohort size of 601 TCGA patients is stated.

statements.text: Drinking LAB-fermented mare milk lowers the burden of resistant bacteria in the human gut.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) are emerging contaminants threatening public health, yet their transmission risk via mare milk products remains understudied.
statements.note: Only the milk products themselves were profiled; no consumption or human gut data appear.

statements.text: Raw, pasteurized and naturally fermented mare milk carried the most pathogens and the highest abundances of ARGs and mobile genetic elements, which LAB inoculation significantly lowered.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The results showed that naturally fermented, raw, and pasteurized mare milk had the highest number of pathogens, relative abundance of ARGs, and relative abundance of mobile genetic elements (MGEs), while LAB inoculation significantly reduced these (p < 0.05).
statements.note: This restates the main comparison between inoculated and non-inoculated milk types.

statements.text: Mobile genetic elements rather than microbes were the key drivers of ARG transmission in mare milk.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Microbes and MGEs jointly drove ARG transmission, with microbes being key.
statements.note: Microbes, not mobile genetic elements, are identified as the key driver.

statements.text: Inoculation with lactic acid bacteria curbed the spread of 11 types of antibiotic resistance gene, among them beta-lactam and multidrug resistance.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: LAB inoculation can effectively inhibit the spread of 11 ARG types, including β-lactam and multidrug resistance, by weakening the co-occurrence network among microbes, ARGs, and MGEs.
statements.note: The count of 11 ARG types and the examples given are reported.

statements.text: Decomposing U. fasciata litter enriched total antibiotic resistance gene abundance by 0.15-0.48% over three months, more strongly for small litter particles.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: U. fasciata decomposition induced the total abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (∑ARGs) significant enrichment by 0.15-0.48% after 3-month operation, and more pronounced effect observed in the small-sized U. fasciata compared to controls
statements.note: The enrichment range and the stronger effect for small-sized litter are both reported.

statements.text: Mantel tests showed total ARG abundance to be more closely tied to the microbial community than to mobile genetic elements or nutrients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: ΣARGs showed stronger associations with mobile genetic elements and nutrient variables at the overall structural level, as revealed by Mantel test analysis, compared to its correspondence with the microbial community.
statements.note: The associations are reversed: ARGs tracked mobile genetic elements and nutrients more strongly than the microbial community.

statements.text: Total nitrogen and phosphorus levels rose with both the amount and the size of the algal litter added.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Results revealed that U. fasciata decomposition significantly increased nutrient concentrations, with total nitrogen and phosphors levels positively correlated with both the quantity and size of U. fasciata litter.
statements.note: Both positive correlations, with litter quantity and with litter size, are reported.

statements.text: Removing Ulva biomass from mariculture ponds reduces sediment ARG abundance below background levels.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This study aimed to ascertain the nutrients release of Ulva (U.) fasciata litter and their effects on antibiotics resistance variation of maricultural sediment.
statements.note: Only litter addition in laboratory microcosms was tested; no removal or field intervention is examined.

statements.text: Lentiviral transfection of these B lymphoma cell lines is highly efficient and consistent.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A couple of B lymphoma cell lines fall into this category where lentiviral transfection becomes inefficient and exhibits variable efficiency.
statements.note: In these lines lentiviral transfection is described as inefficient and variable.

statements.text: Engineering B lymphoma lines to express Cas9 and the mCat-1 receptor allowed gene editing to be delivered by ecotropic gamma-retrovirus.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: By engineering B lymphoma cell lines to express Cas9 and mCat-1, a specific receptor for ecotropic retroviruses, we enable efficient and safe gene editing through ecotropic γ-retrovirus.
statements.note: This is the two-step strategy as described.

statements.text: The same two-step strategy works in primary human B cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: To address this challenge, we have developed a two-step strategy that supports CRISPR-Cas9 through lentivirus and murine ecotropic γ-retrovirus.
statements.note: The strategy is demonstrated only in B lymphoma cell lines; primary cells are not mentioned either way.

statements.text: The approach was demonstrated by producing B lymphoma cell lines that lack IgM.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We demonstrate the efficacy of this method by generating IgM-deficient B lymphoma cell lines.
statements.note: IgM-deficient lines are the stated proof of principle.

statements.text: Tal1 inserts de novo into Arabidopsis thaliana regions occupied by CENH3, and enlarging the CENH3 domain widens where Tal1 integrates.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that the Ty1/Copia element Tal1 (Transposon of Arabidopsis lyrata 1) integrates de novo into regions occupied by CENH3 in Arabidopsis thaliana, and that ectopic expansion of the CENH3 region results in spread of Tal1 integration regions.
statements.note: Both the CENH3-directed integration and the effect of expanding the CENH3 region are reported.

statements.text: Tal1 insertions into centromeres reduce seed set in Arabidopsis thaliana.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Despite the high impact of 'centrophilic' retrotransposons on the paradox of rapid centromere evolution, the mechanisms involved in centromere targeting remain poorly understood in any organism.
statements.note: The work concerns targeting mechanisms; no plant fitness or fertility measurement appears.

statements.text: Both Ty3 and Ty1 long terminal repeat retrotransposons turn over rapidly inside the centromeric tandem repeats of Arabidopsis species.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Here we show that both Ty3 and Ty1 long terminal repeat retrotransposons rapidly turnover within the centromeric TRs of Arabidopsis species.
statements.note: Rapid turnover of both element types within centromeric tandem repeats is the opening result.

statements.text: The integration spectra of chimeric TEs showed that targeting of centromeres versus gene-rich regions stayed fixed throughout the evolution of these elements.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The integration spectra of chimeric TEs reveal the key structural variations responsible for contrasting chromatin-targeting specificities to centromeres versus gene-rich regions, which have recurrently converted during the evolution of these TEs.
statements.note: These specificities are reported to have converted repeatedly, not stayed fixed.

statements.text: Comprehensive genomic profiling reports from 35 veterans with metastatic melanoma were compared against reference database data.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This retrospective review analyzes the comprehensive genomic profiling reports of 35 veterans with metastatic melanoma at a large US Department of Veterans Affairs medical center.
statements.note: The cohort of 35 veterans and the retrospective profiling review are stated.

statements.text: Variants in KMT2C and KMT2D were significantly more frequent in the veterans' melanomas than in the reference databases.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: a significantly lower frequency of variants in ROS1 , GRIN2A , KDR , KMT2C ( MLL3 ), KMT2D ( MLL2 ), LRP1B , PTPRT , PTCH1 , FAT4 , and PREX2
statements.note: Both genes are in the list with significantly lower, not higher, variant frequency.

statements.text: Specific chemical exposures during military service were identified as the cause of the CDKN2A/B enrichment.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Veterans represent a unique patient population with various exposures that may predispose them to cancer. Mutational signatures associated with these exposures are described in other tumor types.
statements.note: Exposures appear only as background; no exposure is linked to a specific variant in this analysis.

statements.text: Tumour mutational burden above 10 mutations per megabase was significantly more frequent in the veterans' melanomas.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a significantly higher frequency of tumor mutational burdens exceeding 10 mutations/megabase
statements.note: The higher frequency above that exact threshold is reported.

statements.text: Glioma patients with higher palmitoylation-related risk scores are the ones more likely to benefit from immunotherapy.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The PRRS model shows promising prospects in predicting the prognosis of glioma patients, and patients with lower PRRS values are more likely to benefit from immunotherapy.
statements.note: It is patients with lower scores who are reported as more likely to benefit.

statements.text: Infiltration by M2-type macrophages and regulatory T cells was greater in Cluster 1 than in Cluster 2.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Additionally, the infiltration levels of M2-type macrophages and regulatory T cells were higher in Cluster 1 than in Cluster 2.
statements.note: This is the reported difference in immune infiltration between the two subtypes.

statements.text: Cluster 1 tumours had higher WHO grade and worse prognosis than Cluster 2 tumours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This study found that compared with glioma patients in Cluster 2, those in Cluster 1 had a higher World Health Organization (WHO) grade and a worse prognosis.
statements.note: Grade and prognosis both differed in this direction between the subtypes.

statements.text: AT-7519, BIX02189 and THZ-2-101-1 cross the blood-brain barrier at therapeutic concentrations.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro drug experiments have confirmed that AT-7519, BIX02189, and THZ-2-101-1 can inhibit glioma cell migration while promoting cell apoptosis.
statements.note: The compounds were assessed by docking, simulation and cell assays; brain penetration is not evaluated.

statements.text: Carriers of DNMT3A-R882 clonal haematopoiesis in this study had higher rates of cardiovascular events.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: CH is linked to pathological immune dysregulation and a greater risk of age-related inflammatory diseases.
statements.note: Disease risk is cited as background; no clinical events in the studied individuals are reported.

statements.text: DNMT3A-R882 shifts the clonal architecture of haematopoiesis towards a youthful phylogenetic structure.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: DNMT3A-R882 reshapes the clonal architecture of haematopoiesis towards an aged phylogenetic structure.
statements.note: The structure is reported as aged, not youthful.

statements.text: Inflammatory transcriptional programmes were dampened in DNMT3A-R882 myeloid progenitors, while the mature neutrophils they produced became proinflammatory.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Whereas DNMT3A-R882 myeloid progenitors display attenuated inflammatory transcriptional programmes, DNMT3A-R882 mature neutrophils acquire proinflammatory and immunomodulatory features typical of maladaptive immunity and CH co-morbidities.
statements.note: The abstract reports this contrast between progenitors and mature neutrophils.

statements.text: DNMT3A-R882 stem cells made less monocytic output but more, and more mature, neutrophil progeny than wild-type stem cells from the same person.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Functionally, DNMT3A-R882 HSCs produce decreased monocytic output but more abundant and mature neutrophil progeny compared to WT HSCs in the same individual.
statements.note: The within-individual comparison with wild-type HSCs gave exactly this output pattern.

statements.text: A Kullback-Leibler divergence computation pinpointed fragment lengths and genomic regions where disease samples diverge from healthy ones from pre-clinical stages onward.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence computation identifies different fragment lengths and areas of the human genome, depending on the stage, for which disease samples, starting from pre-clinical disease stages, diverge from healthy individual samples.
statements.note: This is what the divergence computation is reported to identify.

statements.text: Stage I colorectal cancer sheds enough tumour DNA into circulation for established machine-learning methods to detect it.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In CRC, Stage I disease does not, for the most part, shed any tumor in circulation, making detection difficult for established machine learning (ML) methods.
statements.note: Stage I disease is described as largely not shedding tumour into circulation, which is why those methods struggle.

statements.text: The computer-vision classifier reached higher sensitivity than existing blood tests in a validation cohort.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In a new look to treat such data as grayscale value images, pattern recognition using artificial intelligence could be one approach to classification.
statements.note: Computer vision is put forward as an approach; no classifier performance or comparison is reported.

statements.text: Longitudinal analysis of a patient's own sequencing data detects early-stage neoplasm better than population-based methods.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Longitudinal analysis of patient’s genetic datasets can detect the early stages of neoplasm better than population-based methods.
statements.note: This is the abstract's stated conclusion.

statements.text: CTNNB1 was the most frequently recurrently mutated gene, altered in 7 of the 15 tumours (47%), ahead of TP53 at 33%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: MutSig2CV analysis showed the most significant recurrent somatic mutations in CTNNB1 (47%; 7/15), TP53 (33%; 5/15), SLC7A8 (27%; 4/15), AMOT (20%; 3/15), CLEC11A (20%; 3/15), and ECHDC1 (13%; 2/15) with a q value of ≤ 0.1.
statements.note: The recurrence ranking and the CTNNB1 and TP53 frequencies are reported exactly.

statements.text: Patients whose tumours carried mutational signature 3 responded to platinum chemotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Together, the findings indicated that the crucial role played by these key genetic mutations could be utilized in screening and developing potential targeted therapeutics for TNBC patients.
statements.note: Therapeutic use is only proposed; no treatment or response data are reported.

statements.text: High tumour mutational burden was confined to patients whose tumours showed mutational signature 1.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Interestingly, the high tumor mutational burden was observed specifically in TNBC patients with signature 3.
statements.note: High mutational burden was specific to signature 3, not signature 1.

statements.text: The sequenced triple-negative breast cancer genomes carried about 106 mutations per sample on average.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our data revealed that the TNBC genomes carried an average of ~ 106 mutations per sample.
statements.note: That average mutation count is stated directly.

statements.text: Transposable element polymorphism at the fgf8a locus was reduced in Rhamphochromis compared with the rest of the radiation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Phylogenetic analysis across the radiation reveals elevated transposable element polymorphism at the fgf8a locus in Rhamphochromis , suggesting ongoing regulatory evolution in this clade.
statements.note: Polymorphism at that locus was elevated in Rhamphochromis, not reduced.

statements.text: Transposable elements at the fgf8a locus differ between the two species and act as developmental enhancers in brain and sensory systems.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identify species-specific transposable element repertoires in the Malawi cichlid fgf8a locus that function as developmental enhancers in brain and sensory systems, providing a potential mechanism for expression divergence between species.
statements.note: Species-specific TE repertoires with enhancer function are reported at the fgf8a locus.

statements.text: Fish lacking fgf8a showed altered prey-capture behaviour.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Functional knockout experiments confirm fgf8a ’s essential role in cichlid brain patterning, directly linking this conserved developmental gene to interspecific neuroanatomical variation.
statements.note: Knockouts established a role in brain patterning; no behavioural assay is reported.

statements.text: Forebrain domains in the two cichlid species diverged independently of the other brain regions, a mosaic pattern of brain evolution.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that forebrain domains diverged independently from other brain regions in these species, consistent with mosaic brain evolution.
statements.note: Independent divergence of forebrain domains is the reported result.

statements.text: LL37 strongly boosted type I interferon and pro-inflammatory cytokine output in response to circular DNA, while linearised DNA of the same sequence stayed inert.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Across eccDNA, minicircle and synthetic circular DNA species, LL37 strikingly amplified type I interferon (IFN-I) and pro-inflammatory cytokine production, whereas linearized counterparts of identical sequence remained inactive.
statements.note: The amplification by LL37 and the inactivity of identical linear sequences are both reported.

statements.text: Levels of circulating extrachromosomal circular DNA are elevated in patients with systemic autoimmune disease.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings define a mechanism by which LL37 and circular DNA jointly drive TLR9-dependent IFN-I responses, with implications for autoimmunity, cancer and nucleic acid therapeutics.
statements.note: Autoimmunity is raised only as an implication; no patient samples or eccDNA levels in disease are reported.

statements.text: Surface plasmon resonance showed TLR9 bound circular DNA better than linear DNA, with LL37 binding unchanged between the two.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: surface plasmon resonance revealed enhanced TLR9 binding to circular versus linear DNA, without differential LL37 binding
statements.note: Both the enhanced TLR9 binding and the absence of differential LL37 binding are reported.

statements.text: Chloroquine and the TLR9 antagonist IRS869 left activation by LL37-circular DNA complexes intact.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: LL37-circular DNA complexes signaled through endosomal TLR9, as activation was abrogated by chloroquine and by the TLR9 antagonist IRS869.
statements.note: Activation was abrogated by both agents, which is how TLR9 dependence was established.

statements.text: Methylation markers were most often detectable in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, in 85 of 97 such patients (88%).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Methylation markers were detectable across the PCa disease spectrum, most frequently in metastatic castration-sensitive PCa (mCSPC) (85/97; 88%).
statements.note: The detection counts and percentage for mCSPC are given exactly.

statements.text: Methylation marker levels fell after androgen deprivation therapy in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive disease.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Plasma samples from the initial hospital visit were obtained from 280 participants in the PerPros prostate biobank (Vejle, Denmark), all referred with suspected PCa.
statements.note: Samples came from the initial visit only; no on-treatment follow-up measurement is reported.

statements.text: The panel also separated localised or locally advanced disease from biopsy-confirmed controls well, with an AUC of 0.88.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In contrast, discrimination between localised/locally advanced PCa and patients with biopsy-confirmed controls was limited (AUC 0.56; 95% CI: 0.51-0.61).
statements.note: That discrimination was limited, with an AUC of 0.56 rather than 0.88.

statements.text: The five-marker methylation panel separated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer from controls with an AUC of 0.88.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The ctDNA methylation panel discriminated mCSPC from controls with an AUC (area under the curve) of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.83-0.93).
statements.note: That AUC is the reported performance against biopsy-confirmed controls.

statements.text: In OVSAHO ovarian cancer cells, overexpressing both BRD4 isoforms accelerated tumour growth.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We confirmed these results in OVSAHO ovarian cancer cells, where overexpression of both isoforms significantly reduced tumor growth.
statements.note: Overexpression significantly reduced tumour growth in those cells.

statements.text: Open-reading-frame screen data from 16 cancer cell lines showed that overexpressing either the long or the short BRD4 isoform is toxic to cancer cell growth.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we first leveraged open-reading-frame (ORF) screen data from 16 cancer cell lines, where we observed that overexpression of BRD4-long and BRD4-short isoforms is toxic for cancer cell growth
statements.note: The number of cell lines and the toxicity of both isoforms are reported.

statements.text: Focal deletions in BRD4 regulatory regions rescued ovarian carcinoma cells from the toxicity of BRD4 overexpression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We finally show that these focal deletions rescue ovarian carcinoma cells from the toxicity effects associated with gene overexpression, suggesting that global BRD4 gene expression levels must be fine tuned to ensure proper cancer cell proliferation.
statements.note: This rescue effect is the study's closing experimental result.

statements.text: BRD4 focal deletions predict resistance to BET inhibitors in ovarian cancer.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our study provides experimental evidence for BRD4 deletions constituting the first example of a driver SV alteration reducing toxicity in cancer, therefore expanding the landscape of cancer progression mechanisms.
statements.note: No drug treatment or inhibitor response is tested anywhere in the study.

statements.text: Filtering 367 preliminary candidate pairs left 325 final synthetic anti-metastasis pairs.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified 325 final SAM pairs from 367 preliminary pairs.
statements.note: Both pair counts are stated.

statements.text: Patients with many co-impaired or co-inactivated SAM pairs had shorter overall survival and more metastasis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We found that patients with a high number of co-impairment or -inactivation of SAM pairs showed improved overall survival and reduced metastasis.
statements.note: Both directions are inverted: such patients had improved survival and reduced metastasis.

statements.text: Trametinib reduced metastatic spread in melanoma mouse models in this study.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Candidate anti-metastatic drugs for melanoma were identified through LINCS-based gene signature analysis, network analysis, and literature review.
statements.note: The five compounds came from computational analysis and literature; no animal experiment is reported.

statements.text: A machine-learning model on SAM gene features separated primary from metastatic melanoma with an AUROC of 0.940, beating models from other metastasis-associated genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The ML model based on SAM gene features accurately distinguished primary from metastases melanoma samples (AUROC: 0.940; HR: 0.724), outperforming models built from other known melanoma metastasis-associated genes.
statements.note: The AUROC value and the comparison with other gene-set models are reported.

statements.text: The diploid progenitors of Eutrema japonicum split roughly 2 million years ago, while the allotetraploid hybridisation forming the species happened about 0.268 million years ago.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The diploid progenitors of E. japonicum diverged approximately 2 MYA, while the allotetraploid hybridization event that formed E. japonicum occurred more recently (~ 0.268 MYA).
statements.note: Both dates are given with these values.

statements.text: Long terminal repeat retrotransposons are more abundant in the dominant subgenome of wasabi than in the other subgenome.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We also characterized transposable elements, including long terminal repeat retrotransposons (LTR-RTs), and analyzed gene expression patterns between subgenomes to further understand genome evolution and functional differentiation in E. japonicum.
statements.note: Transposable elements were catalogued and expression compared between subgenomes, but TE abundance per subgenome is not reported.

statements.text: Wasabi's glucosinolate gene profile shows an expanded ESM1 family alongside a contracted ESP gene, giving a high ESM1:ESP copy ratio.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This profile is characterized by a significant expansion of the epithiospecifier-modifying protein (ESM1) gene family, which promotes pungent isothiocyanate formation, and a contraction of the competing epithiospecifier protein (ESP) gene.
statements.note: The expansion, the contraction and the resulting high copy ratio are all reported.

statements.text: After whole-genome duplication the wasabi genome remained largely unrearranged and showed no subgenome dominance.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Following this whole-genome duplication, its genome stabilized through extensive chromosomal rearrangements and subgenome dominance.
statements.note: Stabilisation is reported to have proceeded through extensive rearrangements and subgenome dominance.

statements.text: Preoperative ctDNA analysis detected a clinically relevant molecular alteration in 29 patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Twenty-nine patients were found to be positive for one of the clinically relevant molecular alterations detected by NGS, at preoperative (T0) ctDNA analysis.
statements.note: Twenty-nine positive patients at the preoperative timepoint are reported.

statements.text: On univariate analysis, total tumour size above 60 mm showed no significant association with recurrence.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: At univariate analysis, total tumor size bigger than 60 mm (p = 0.046, HR 2.486) and postoperative persistence of ctDNA molecular signature (p = 0.024, HR 2.831) were significantly associated with recurrence.
statements.note: Tumour size above 60 mm was significantly associated with recurrence on univariate analysis.

statements.text: In multivariable Cox regression, postoperative persistence of the ctDNA signature was the only factor still associated with recurrence, with a hazard ratio of 2.766.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Multivariable Cox Regression analysis showed that only postoperative persistence of ctDNA molecular signature was associated with recurrence (p = 0.027, HR 2.766).
statements.note: Persistence was the sole surviving predictor, with that hazard ratio.

statements.text: Adjuvant chemotherapy after resection cleared the persistent ctDNA signature in most patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Patients underwent liquid biopsy from peripheral blood samples before and after surgery.
statements.note: Sampling was pre- and post-surgery; no effect of adjuvant treatment on the ctDNA signature is reported.

statements.text: Recent transposon bursts in Vickermania species are linked to increased virulence in their insect hosts.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We found evidence of recent transposon activity in most species, with notable bursts in the Vickermania, Lafontella, Porcisia and Angomonas spp.
statements.note: Bursts of activity are reported, but no host phenotype or virulence is examined.

statements.text: Repeat content was predicted and transposable elements manually curated across the genomes of 57 trypanosomatids.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We predicted repeat content and manually curated TEs across the genomes of 57 trypanosomatids, shedding light on their proportions, diversity and dynamics.
statements.note: The number of genomes analysed is stated directly.

statements.text: The analysis produced 214 TE consensus models, with TE abundance ranging from 0.1% to 7.2% across the genomes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our analysis yielded 214 TE consensus sequence models across the dataset, with abundance ranging from 0.1% to 7.2%.
statements.note: The model count and abundance range are reported exactly.

statements.text: The four known TE clades were restricted to a few trypanosomatid lineages.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We confirmed that the 4 TE clades have colonized virtually all lineages of trypanosomatids, potentially playing a role in shaping their genome architecture.
statements.note: The four clades were found to have colonised virtually all trypanosomatid lineages.
